dod_intent_evidence: $2,749,999 Air Force Phase II SBIR (2022) for a 'fieldable' warfighter TBI Tracker, corroborated by LinkedIn about's own claim of 'funding from the Department of Defense' — SBIR abstract section. Note: a 'Spark Biomedical Partners With Air Force' news item in this pack is about a different company (Spark Biomedical, not Spark Neuro) and was disregarded per instructions.
score_evidence: "Always-On Intelligence / Surfaces what matters — proactively." (Spark Predict platform) → lab_language_intensity (cloud-native, always-on framing carried across the company's newer product line, with zero operational/field grounding)

"With the push of a button, the tool automatically runs the test protocols and in a matter of seconds, generates an easy-to-understand report." → deployment_awareness_absence (frames field use as consumer-simple, doesn't address motion artifact, electrode contact, or calibration realities of EEG in the field)

blind_spots.blind_spot: The company's newer flagship product (Spark Predict) is built entirely around 'Always-On Intelligence' and continuous cloud data streaming, a model at odds with the point-of-care fielding claimed for the AF TBI Tracker.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Point-of-care testing after a head injury in the field can't depend on always-on cloud connectivity; a DDIL environment breaks a platform architected around continuous data streaming and query-in-seconds responsiveness.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Company has pivoted its core business toward civilian payer/provider healthcare analytics; the DoD TBI program appears to be a smaller, separate legacy line not integrated into that roadmap.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Always-On Intelligence Surfaces what matters — proactively.

blind_spots.blind_spot: The TBI Tracker abstract markets a 'push of a button' simplicity that glosses over EEG's well-known sensitivity to motion artifact, sweat, and electrode placement.
blind_spots.operator_reality: EEG signal quality is famously sensitive to motion, sweat, and electrode contact — an untrained E-5 in the field, not a technician in a controlled setting, is who has to get a clean read, and nothing in the abstract addresses that failure mode.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Abstract is written to sell ease-of-use and speed to a program office, not to work through field signal-quality engineering.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: With the push of a button, the tool automatically runs the test protocols and in a matter of seconds, generates an easy-to-understand report.

blind_spots.blind_spot: No mention anywhere (site, abstract, LinkedIn about) of who owns sustainment, calibration, or software updates for a fielded EEG device once it leaves the Mayo Clinic research collaboration and reaches a deployed unit.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Institutional-research credibility (Mayo Clinic, DoD, NIH funding) doesn't answer who calibrates or maintains the device at a forward operating location with no biomedical technician on staff.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Company's institutional partnerships are framed as clinical/research validation, not field sustainment planning.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: SPARK Neuro has a history of collaborating with prestigious institutions like the Mayo Clinic and Johns Hopkins Medicine and has earned funding from the Department of Defense and the National Institutes of Health.

opener_hook: SPARK Neuro's Air Force-funded TBI Tracker promises point-of-care fielding, while its newer Spark Predict platform is built entirely around 'always-on' cloud intelligence.
what_they_do: AI-powered EEG platform for dementia diagnosis aimed at civilian healthcare payers/providers, with a separate Air Force-funded 'fieldable' TBI Tracker for warfighter brain-injury monitoring.
